<description>
{
 "summary": "Fixes two regressions in the bitcoin-cli lightweight HTTP client introduced by the removal of libevent. It treats HTTP responses with Content-Length: 0 as complete instead of waiting for a connection close, and restores -rpcclienttimeout to act as an idle timeout per socket read rather than a fixed overall phase deadline.",
 "problem": "In bitcoin-cli, responses with Content-Length: 0 (such as RPC authentication errors) fell into the branch for lengthless responses and hung until the server closed the connection. Additionally, -rpcclienttimeout was altered from an inactivity timeout to a strict phase deadline, causing large or slow RPC responses to be aborted even while incoming data was actively arriving.",
 "evidence": [
  "Post-merge review by b-l-u-e on #34342 pointed out the Content-Length handling flaw: 'b-l-u-e found this in post-merge review in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34342#discussion_r3358700705'",
  "PR description highlights that without resetting on data arrival, '-rpcclienttimeout no longer measures real idle time... so a large/slow response could be cut off while data still arrives.'"
 ],

<category name="tools" title="Tools and scripts">
## Covers

Command-line tools other than the node and its RPC client, and the
scripts under contrib: `bitcoin-tx`, `bitcoin-util`, the offline
`bitcoin-wallet` tool, the `bitcoin` wrapper, seed and asmap
generation, signet tooling, tracing scripts, and developer helper
scripts. Build and release scripts are build; test helpers are tests.
The Scripts and tools label is a strong prior.

## What matters here

Tools that operators and downstream projects depend on first: seed
generation, asmap, signet, and the wallet tool affect real deployments.
Then correctness of any tool that touches keys or transactions. Then
developer productivity tools that many contributors use. Then niche or
single-user scripts, which rank low regardless of size.
